answer: Picture each new agent posting a bond that stays locked for months, like sediment slowly pressing into shale. Its reputation grows only as the bond ages and peers attest to useful work, so a fresh identity carries almost no signal. An attacker hoping to flood the network with a raven-black swarm of fake accounts must lock capital for every one of them and wait. If any are caught colluding, their bonds are slashed. Spinning up a thousand sybils stops being free and becomes a slow, expensive gamble.
